metadata.title: Staatsbürgerinnen und Staatsbürger von morgen: Zur Wirksamkeit politischer Bildung in der Schweiz. Ein Vergleich mit 37 anderen Ländern
metadata.venue: ICCS – International Civic and Citizenship Education Study

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses ICCS 2009 sampling with a multi-stage stratified design: schools are stratified by school type and language region, then selected with PPS (probability proportional to size), followed by random selection of intact classes. Participation requirements for inclusion in analyses are defined at both school and student levels (at least 85% at each level, or 75% combined), and in some cases full participation is used when the target number of schools/students is small. The report presents international scaling and country comparisons using ICCS score scales (e.g., political knowledge and understanding with an international mean of 500 and SD of 100; attitudinal scales with international mean 50 and SD 10), but it does not specify the exact weight variable names used in the international database. Because the manuscript does not describe whether analysts applied student sampling weights and/or replicate weights, the weighting approach should follow ICCS standard procedures for complex survey inference when re-analyzing the microdata.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This report focuses on ICCS 2009 score scaling and descriptive/cross-national comparisons of political knowledge and multiple attitudinal/behavioral scales, but it does not document any Plausible Values (PV) workflow or PV-based achievement score generation/combination strategy. In addition, the outcomes emphasized here are presented as scaled scores and percentages derived from ICCS instruments rather than as PV-based cognitive achievement estimates with an explicit PV combining rule. Therefore, PV handling and missing-data handling are not reported in a way that can be mapped to the PV/missing-data schema for empirical predictive modeling.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The target population is students in Grade 8; if the average age in a country is below 13.5 years, Grade 9 students are used instead. The sampling is multi-stage and stratified: schools are stratified by school type and language region, then selected using PPS (probability proportional to size), excluding schools attended exclusively by students with intellectual disabilities and excluding very small schools (fewer than 6 students in the relevant grade). Within selected schools, intact classes are randomly selected (typically one class per school). For a country to be included in analyses, participation thresholds are required at both school and student levels (at least 85% at each level, or 75% combined). In Switzerland, the report states that 2,924 students from 156 classes/schools participated, with an average age of 14.7 years.

data.outcome_summary: This ICCS 2009 report compares political education outcomes across 38 participating countries, focusing on students aged 14–15 (typically Grade 8; Grade 9 when the country’s average age is below 13.5). The study uses a 45-minute test with 80 items (multiple-choice and open-response) to measure political knowledge and understanding, scaled to an international mean of 500 (SD=100) with three performance levels (cut points at 395, 479, 563). Students also complete a 40-minute student questionnaire capturing attitudes, beliefs, interests, trust, and intended/actual civic engagement; several attitudinal scales are scaled to an international mean of 50 (SD=10). Sampling is multi-stage and stratified (school type and language region), with PPS school selection and random class selection, and countries are included only when participation thresholds are met. The report provides cross-national comparisons and Switzerland-specific results (e.g., Switzerland’s political knowledge mean of 531 vs. ICCS mean 500) but does not present an ML predictive modeling pipeline or PV/missing-data handling documentation suitable for PV-based empirical ML extraction.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is treated as a framework/technical comparative report rather than an empirical ML paper: the manuscript reports descriptive and comparative results from ICCS 2009 (scaled scores, percentages, and performance levels) without training or evaluating machine learning models. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques, PV combining rules, and missing-data handling for predictive estimation are not applicable in the schema sense. The report is still empirical in the sense of survey-based measurement, but it does not provide the ML-specific methodological details (e.g., model training, validation metrics, PV strategy for achievement DVs) required by the predictive ML extraction rules.
